Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of
neck and back strain. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported impact,
and the symptoms described fit that force well. Over the course of 25 visits, care
proceeded along a typical trajectory of manual therapy, targeted exercise, and home
stretching, with visit frequency tapering as pain and mobility improved. Physical
examination revealed some objective findings, including reduced cervical range of
motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, while other provocative tests and
neurological screening were within normal limits. The patient reports a remote history
of a minor strain in the same region that resolved completely without lasting
limitation, and this was considered in the assessment. Billing records reflect single
entries for each service without duplicated charges. At discharge, the patient was
improving and was advised to continue an independent home exercise program.
